notes.text: The buggy program's output ("1,8,27,64" twice) relies on the .NET 10 SharedArrayPool implementation detail that a returned array is stored in a per-thread (TLS) slot and the next Rent of the same bucket on the same thread returns it. The buggy code is not run against an expect value (find-bug only checks fixedSource), but the prompt states this output; confirm with a real run.
Claim that ArrayPool<int>.Shared.Rent(4) returns an array of length 16 (smallest bucket) on .NET 10; based on the SharedArrayPool bucket sizes starting at 16.
fixedExpect assumes the two Rent calls in the fixed code return distinct arrays (pool empty at start, so both allocate new arrays) and the output is exactly "1,4,9,16\n1,8,27,64".
Russian explanation contains the phrase about the array the pool "уже не принадлежит ему"; the owner may want to smooth this sentence (meaning: the pool now considers the array free).
